facts.text: Wilbraham first drew attention in 1636 when William Pynchon bought the area from the Nipmuc, extending to the foot of the Wilbraham Mountain Range by 1674.
The Underground Railroad threaded through Wilbraham, with several Main Street houses and Wilbraham Mountain homes serving as secret stations.
Wilbraham hosts New England’s oldest Methodist meeting house and the Wilbraham & Monson Academy, founded in 1804, both anchoring the town’s historic center.
Rice’s Fruit Farm, opened in 1894, remains a historic New England family‑run stand offering breakfast, coffee, pies, apples and ice cream.
Wilbraham’s name traces back to Wilburga’s homestead, the daughter of King Penda, whose land gave the town’s original designation.
